author: Sam Graham
title: Roanoke County set to award $108k to local businesses through BEAP grant - NewsBreak
text:
By Sam Graham ,
1 hours ago
ROANOKE COUNTY, Va. ( WFXR ) — Last year, the Roanoke County economic development authority (EDA) piloted its Business Equipment Acquisition Program (BEAP) as a way to support local businesses by providing matching funds on equipment purchases.
“We want to support our businesses of all sizes,” said Roanoke County director of economic development Megan Baker. “We want to say it as a thank you for doing business in Roanoke County, choosing our community to do business, to grow in.”
Offering a 50 percent match on business equipment purchases up to $20,000, the funds will boost both small and large local businesses.
“For us, it’s a matter of replacing equipment, but also upgrading other equipment,” said Salem Animal Hospital medical director and co-owner Dr. Rich Bryant. “So, one, to maintain our capabilities, but also to enhance our skill sets and our future capabilities with the equipment that we need.”
The Salem Animal Hospital is one of 14 businesses set to benefit from the grant this year.
Bryant says the animal hospital, like many other small businesses across the country, has experienced a challenging year.
He says the grant funding will provide a significant boost toward purchasing upgrades to dental surgical equipment and oxygen cages, along with other direct-care equipment.
“I think for every business, every industry, this has been a tough year,” said Bryant. “Everybody’s watching their pennies very tightly. So, to have an opportunity like this to be able to invest in equipment that can increase your level of service and your level of care. We wouldn’t be able to do it otherwise.”
Businesses across Roanoke County and Vinton were eligible to apply for the grant, and those that did were scored and ultimately selected based on a set of criteria ranging from business size to expected impact of the funding.
